title: Best Dehumidifier for 1500 Sq Ft (2026): 35 or 50 Pints?
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for 1,500 Square Feet
dek: At 1,500 square feet you sit right on the line between a mid-size and a full basement unit. Here's how to tell which side you're on.
description: The best dehumidifier for 1,500 square feet (and 1,200 sq ft), sized by dampness with our chart: when 35 pints is enough, when to buy 50 and when to go ducted.
intro: Shopping for a **dehumidifier for 1,500 square feet** puts you in an awkward spot on most sizing charts. It's the upper edge of what a 35-pint unit can handle and the lower edge of where a 50-pint basement model becomes the obvious choice. Pick wrong in one direction and the unit runs all day without reaching your target; pick wrong in the other and you've paid for capacity you don't use.

The tiebreaker is almost never the floor area. It's how damp the space is, whether it's one open room or several closed ones, and whether there's a drain nearby. A 1,500-square-foot finished lower level that just smells a little stale is a very different job from a 1,500-square-foot unfinished basement where the walls sweat every July.

Below, we lay out the sizing math from our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) for 1,200 to 1,500 square feet, then match five Amazon-available dehumidifiers to the situations you're most likely to have.
topPicksLead: For most 1,500-square-foot basements, the **Midea Cube 50** is the best fit: a full 50 pints a day under the current DOE test, a big base reservoir and a humidistat that cycles off once it reaches your target.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for 1,500 sq ft

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compared current DOE 2019 capacity ratings, ENERGY STAR efficiency listings and manufacturer manuals for humidistat range, drainage and coverage claims, checked the CPSC database for recalls and read owner reviews for recurring problems such as failing pumps, leaking buckets and sensors that read well off a separate hygrometer.

Because 1,500 square feet sits between two size tiers, we deliberately chose one strong pick on each side — a 35-pint unit for moderately damp spaces and 50-pint units for damp basements — plus a pump model and a ducted option for whole-house problems. Every pick is available on Amazon.

sections.heading: What to look for in a 1,500 sq ft dehumidifier

items.label: A DOE 2019 rating, not a marketing number
items.text: Labels like “for up to 4,500 sq ft” or saturation pints inflate capacity. Compare current DOE pints across brands.

items.label: A set-percentage humidistat
items.text: The unit should stop at your number. That's what lets a 50-pint machine work in a space that only sometimes needs 50 pints.

items.label: A drain plan
items.text: A 1,500 sq ft basement in July can outpace any bucket. Run a gravity hose to a floor drain or buy a pump model.

items.label: Efficiency
items.text: A unit holding 1,500 square feet can run hundreds of hours a season. ENERGY STAR models cost less over the years.

items.label: A layout check
items.text: One open rectangle suits one unit. Closed rooms off a hallway may need two units or a ducted system.

sections.heading: 35 pints or 50 pints for 1,500 square feet?

blocks.text: If you're torn between sizes, four quick questions settle it. Answer yes to two or more and buy the 50-pint unit.

items: **Is it below grade?** Basements pull moisture through the foundation all season.
**Do you see condensation?** Sweating pipes, damp concrete or fogged windows mean you're in the very-damp tier or worse.
**Is there a dryer, shower or sump in the space?** Each adds a steady moisture load.
**Is the ceiling taller than 8 feet, or the space open to a stairwell?** More air volume means more water to remove.

blocks.text: Sizing up costs less than you'd think. A larger unit reaches the target faster and then cycles off, so its total runtime can be shorter than an undersized unit that never quite catches up — provided its humidistat works. Our [best 50-pint dehumidifier](/best/best-50-pint-dehumidifier/) guide covers more options in that class.
What about a 1,200 sq ft basement?

Our size guide uses exactly this example: a 1,200-square-foot basement with condensation on the foundation walls needs 30–40 pints, so the Cube 35 is a good fit. Add a dryer venting into the space and step up to a 50-pint unit.

sections.heading: A 1,500 sq ft house or crawl space

blocks.text: A whole 1,500-square-foot house is a different job from a 1,500-square-foot basement. A portable dehumidifier can only dry air that reaches it, so bedrooms with closed doors stay humid while the room with the unit is dry. In a humid climate, a ducted unit like the Aprilaire E080 — or simply letting your central AC run longer cycles — is usually the better answer. For the trade-offs, see our [best whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) guide.

Crawl spaces need a purpose-built unit with low-temperature defrost and a pump, not a portable. Recent residential codes size dehumidifiers for unvented crawls at 70 pints a day per 1,000 square feet, which works out to about 105 pints for a 1,500-square-foot crawl. Our [encapsulated crawl space dehumidifier](/best/best-encapsulated-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) guide walks through that math.

blocks.title: About those “1,500 sq ft” labels
blocks.text: Coverage claims on listings assume mild dampness and ideal airflow. A unit sold for “1,500 sq ft” may be undersized for a damp basement of that size. Check its DOE pint rating against the chart above instead.

sections.heading: What it costs to run a dehumidifier for 1,500 sq ft

blocks.text: Running cost depends on how long the unit runs, which depends on dampness and your humidistat setting more than on square footage. ENERGY STAR estimates the Cube 50 uses about 515 kWh a year; at roughly 18 cents per kWh, that's in the neighborhood of $90 a year under its assumptions. A unit cycling to hold 50% in a moderately damp space will use less; one running continuously in a wet basement, more. Our [electricity use guide](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) shows how to estimate your own bill.

Decide how damp your 1,500 square feet is before you decide how big a dehumidifier to buy. For most basements and lower levels, the **Midea Cube 50** is the right call. If the space is only musty, the **Midea Cube 35** is enough. Choose the **Frigidaire FFAP5033W1** when there's no floor drain, the **Honeywell TP50AWKN** to save money, and the **Aprilaire E080** when the whole house needs drying. Smaller or larger space? See our [1,000 sq ft](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-1000-sq-ft/) and [2,000 sq ft](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-2000-sq-ft/) guides.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for 1,500 square feet?
faqs.a: Between 25 and 50 pints a day under the current DOE rating, depending on dampness: about 25–30 pints for a musty space, 30–40 for one with condensation and 40–50 for seepage or standing water. Most 1,500 sq ft basements do best with a 50-pint unit.

faqs.q: Is a 35-pint dehumidifier enough for 1,500 sq ft?
faqs.a: For a moderately damp, open space such as a finished lower level, yes. For an unfinished basement with condensation or seepage, step up to 50 pints so the unit can reach your target and cycle off.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for 1,200 sq ft?
faqs.a: Roughly 25–30 pints if it's only musty and 30–40 pints if you see condensation. A 1,200 sq ft basement with a dryer or shower in it should get a 50-pint unit.

faqs.q: Can one dehumidifier handle a 1,500 sq ft house?
faqs.a: Only if the space is open enough for air to reach the unit. A portable won't dry closed bedrooms down the hall. For whole-house humidity, consider a ducted unit such as the Aprilaire E080.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier for a 1,500 sq ft crawl space?
faqs.a: Use a crawl-space unit, not a portable. Recent codes call for 70 pints a day per 1,000 square feet of unvented crawl, or about 105 pints for 1,500 square feet; manufacturer ratings for tightly sealed crawls are more generous.

faqs.q: Is the Midea Cube a good dehumidifier for 1,500 sq ft?
faqs.a: Yes. The Cube 50 suits damp 1,500 sq ft basements, and the Cube 35 suits moderately damp spaces of that size. Both have set-percentage humidistats, base reservoirs and gravity-drain options.
